Conditional power at an interim look

Source: R/ms_cond_power.R
ms_cond_power.Rd

Computes, for a design with one endpoint, the probability that the trial crosses an efficacy bound at a later look, given the standardized log-rank statistic observed at an interim look, under a chosen distribution of the statistics.

Usage

ms_cond_power(
  x,
  look,
  z,
  under = c("design", "null", "trend", "hr", "scenario"),
  hr = NULL,
  scenario = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An ms_power object with one endpoint (from ms_power or ms_size).

look

Interim look at which z is observed (from 1 to the number of looks minus 1).

z

Observed standardized log-rank statistic at look (positive when the treatment is better), or the observed statistics at the looks 1 to look. It must be below the efficacy bounds and, with binding futility bounds, not below the futility bounds.

under

Distribution of the statistics: "design", "null", "trend", "hr" or "scenario" (see Details).

hr

Hazard ratio (treatment versus control) for under = "hr".

scenario

An ms_scenario object with the allocation and accrual of the design scenario, for under = "scenario".

Value

An object of class ms_cond_power, a list with

cond_power

The conditional power.

cond_power_nonbinding

The conditional power without the futility bounds of the later interim looks.

looks

A data frame with one row per later look: look, time and events (calendar time and expected events of the tested endpoint under the distribution of under), the bounds z_upper and z_lower, the conditional mean and standard deviation of the statistic (cond_mean, cond_sd), the conditional probabilities of stopping for efficacy and for futility at the look (prob_upper, prob_lower) and the cumulative conditional power cum_upper.

look, z, under

The inputs.

hr

The hazard ratio of "trend" and "hr" (NA otherwise).

Details

At the interim look j with the observed statistic z, the statistics of the later looks given \(Z_j = z\) have the conditional normal distribution of the joint normal distribution of the statistics chosen by under. The conditional power is the probability that, at some later look k, the statistic crosses the efficacy bound after the statistics of the looks between j and k have stayed between the futility and efficacy bounds, as in gsCP() of gsDesign; cond_power_nonbinding leaves out the futility bounds of the later interim looks (a trial that continues despite non-binding futility bounds). The bounds are those of the design (x$looks). When the events observed at the interim look differ from those planned, the bounds of the design no longer apply: compute the design again with ms_power with looks that give the observed events and the remaining planned events, and use the new design.

With z of length look, the statistics of the looks 1 to look are all conditioned on. For statistics with independent increments (variance = "null" of ms_test, except OS with switching from a calendar time) the result is the same as with the statistic of the look alone; with "alternative" and "studentized" it can differ. In both cases the conditioning does not use the fact that the trial did not stop at the earlier looks.

The distributions (under):

"design"

The mean and covariance of the statistics under the design scenario (x$mean, x$sigma).

"null"

Mean zero and the correlations under the null scenario (x$sigma_null), at the looks of the type I error (x$looks_null); the result is the conditional type I error.

"trend"

The current trend: a constant hazard ratio exp(-z / sqrt(p0 p1 d_j)) estimated from z, where p0 and p1 are the allocation probabilities and d the expected events of the tested endpoint at the looks of the design, so that the mean of the statistic at look k is z sqrt(d_k / d_j), with the correlations sqrt(d_j / d_k) used for the bounds.

"hr"

A constant hazard ratio hr: the mean at look k is -log(hr) sqrt(p0 p1 d_k), with the correlations sqrt(d_j / d_k).

"scenario"

The mean and covariance under scenario, with the approximations of the test of the design; the event-driven looks take place when the expected events of their trigger endpoint reach the event targets of the design (x$targets), also when the final look of the design is fixed by followup, and the calendar-driven looks keep their times.

"trend" and "hr" assume proportional hazards (the Schoenfeld approximation) and do not use the shape of the hazard ratio of the design scenario, such as a delayed effect; "scenario" does.

References

Ortega-Villa AM, Grieco MC, Rubenstein K, Wang J, Proschan MA (2025). Futility monitoring in clinical trials. Statistics in Medicine, 44, e70157.

See also

ms_power, gs_prob

Examples

ctl <- ms_model(death = log(2) / 12)
trt <- ms_model(death = 0.7 * log(2) / 12)
scn <- ms_scenario(ctl, trt, accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 20))
des <- ms_power(scn, n = 400, looks = ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.5, 1)),
                test = ms_test(), events = 300)
ms_cond_power(des, look = 1, z = 1.2)
#> Conditional power of a group sequential log-rank design
#>   Observed at look 1: z = 1.2
#>   Distribution: design scenario
#>   Conditional power: 0.7269
#>   Without the futility bounds of the later interim looks: 0.7269
#>  look  time events z_upper z_lower cond_mean cond_sd prob_upper prob_lower
#>     2 39.67    300   1.969   1.969     2.393  0.7032     0.7269     0.2731
#>  cum_upper
#>     0.7269
ms_cond_power(des, look = 1, z = 1.2, under = "trend")
#> Conditional power of a group sequential log-rank design
#>   Observed at look 1: z = 1.2
#>   Distribution: current trend (hazard ratio 0.822)
#>   Conditional power: 0.3505
#>   Without the futility bounds of the later interim looks: 0.3505
#>  look  time events z_upper z_lower cond_mean cond_sd prob_upper prob_lower
#>     2 39.67    300   1.969   1.969     1.697  0.7071     0.3505     0.6495
#>  cum_upper
#>     0.3505
ms_cond_power(des, look = 1, z = 1.2, under = "hr", hr = 0.8)
#> Conditional power of a group sequential log-rank design
#>   Observed at look 1: z = 1.2
#>   Distribution: hazard ratio 0.8
#>   Conditional power: 0.4139
#>   Without the futility bounds of the later interim looks: 0.4139
#>  look  time events z_upper z_lower cond_mean cond_sd prob_upper prob_lower
#>     2 39.67    300   1.969   1.969     1.815  0.7071     0.4139     0.5861
#>  cum_upper
#>     0.4139
